posts.title: When Crisis Comes: Danger or Opportunity?
posts.description: A crisis consists of two elements: danger and opportunity. Saul looked at Goliath and saw a threat, but David looked through the eyes of faith and saw an opportunity.
posts.content:
A crisis consists of two elements: danger and opportunity. Thus, when we face a crisis, our future is determined by what we look at.

Saul looked at Goliath and saw a threat, but David looked through the eyes of faith and saw an opportunity.

Everything that comes our way is an opportunity from God to establish and strengthen us.

As it is written in Romans 8:28:

> "And we know that all things work together for good to those who love God, to those who are the called according to His purpose."

When crisis strikes today, will you focus on the danger like Saul, or look through the eyes of faith like David to seize the opportunity God is giving you?

posts.title: the key that unlocks the gates of heaven
posts.description:
The mindset of "Me first" creates hell,
while the attitude of "You first" transforms that place into heaven.
posts.content:
In hell, a grand feast was laid out,
yet everyone was starving and bone-thin.
Their spoons were much longer than their arms,
so even when they scooped up food, they could not put it into their own mouths.

In heaven, under the exact same conditions,
the people looked healthy, radiant, and happy.
They were using those same long spoons
to feed the person sitting across the table.

Heaven and hell are not defined by our circumstances.

The mindset of "Me first" creates hell,
while the attitude of "You first" transforms that place into heaven.

Today, an attitude of heart that chooses "God first" instead of "Me first"
will become the key that unlocks the gates of heaven for you.

Do you hold that key in your heart today?
